rulings.reason: The instruction explicitly disclaims length as such and asks the judge to decide whether each setup clause is reverse-engineered from the punchline or does independent work, which requires reading the content and judging comedic craft. A high score is evidence about how well the joke is built, not merely about how long it is.

Typo and grammar counting scores an orthographic production habit of whoever posted the item, and a clean joke is not thereby a funnier joke; most of its variance is care-in-posting, not humor. Mixed because errors that garble the operative pun, as the instruction notes, genuinely degrade the reading and so can reduce actual funniness.

Scoring timeless versus news-cycle subject matter is a topic and temporal marker: it reads what the joke is about and when it was written, not how well it works as a joke. Mixed because universal subject matter plausibly does carry genuinely broader relatable appeal to a voting crowd.

The instruction explicitly directs the judge not to reward or punish quality and to score only apparent circulation age, making it a provenance fingerprint of where the text came from rather than evidence about the joke itself. Mixed because reader over-familiarity with a warhorse plausibly does depress the crowd's funniness verdict.
